answer: A proposed lagoon exchange disables earning keys that fail to relay 600 MB of fresh data each minute; every extra alias owes another 600 MB/min. Testers send a different random stream per key to its assigned receiver, whose signed, timed byte counts gate renewal. A raven courier cannot bridge ten aliases with one completed transfer: ten require 6 GB/min. Independent receivers and per-key stream tags prevent receipt reuse. Honest metering is essential; bandwidth-rich farms can still buy many slots.
